title: Rank-one subrank obstruction for the Möbius–Mersenne ladder

concepts.label: uniform Möbius–Mersenne floor
concepts.note: The rational lower endpoint for ladder rungs r≥3.

concepts.label: rank-one strict-subrank quotient
concepts.note: The finite-prefix monomial quotient compared with the second ladder rung.

concepts.label: positive finite averaging
concepts.note: Nonempty strictly positive weighted averages of admissible rank-one quotients.

concepts.label: restricted rational linear form
concepts.note: The integer-linear-form consequence for exact rational realisations from this quotient family.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every Möbius–Mersenne ladder rung r≥3, 1429/1512≤Theta_r.
statement_nodes.engine: two-atom decomposition, geometric tail enclosure, and elementary rational comparison
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A tuned elementary corollary of the already-authored two-atom split and geometric tail bound; no novelty claim is made for 1429/1512.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The lower floor is not claimed sharp and proves no rationality or irrationality statement.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every e≥1 and prefix length Y≥4, 1/480 < mobiusMersennePrefix(Y,e+2)^2 / mobiusMersennePrefix(Y,2e+2) - Theta_2. Thus this exact rank-one quotient family stays a uniform positive distance above the #249 ladder target.
statement_nodes.engine: uniform rung floor, finite-prefix error control, rung upper bounds, and the estimate Theta_2<8/9
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The paper presents this family-level exclusion as a candidate new barrier. External priority review has not been completed, so no established novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The barrier applies only to this quotient with e≥1 and Y≥4. It does not exclude higher-rank determinants, other exponent patterns, nonlinear coordinates, or other finite-linear constructions, and it does not prove the target irrational.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Every nonempty finite weighted average of admissible rank-one quotients, with every weight strictly positive, remains more than 1/480 above Theta_2.
statement_nodes.engine: strictly positive finite averaging of the pointwise uniform margin
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Positive averaging preserves a uniform pointwise lower bound; the value lies in the exact scoping to the admissible family.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem requires a finite nonempty family and strictly positive weights. It does not cover signed weights, cancellation, zero-weight degeneracies, or infinite combinations.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If an admissible rank-one quotient is exactly p/q with q≥1, then q/480 < |q*Theta_2-p|.
statement_nodes.engine: substitution of the exact rational representation and multiplication by the positive denominator
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Algebraic transport of the proved quotient gap under an exact rational representation; no general irrationality-measure claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem assumes an exact equality with p/q and neither produces such a representation nor assumes gcd(p,q)=1. Its bound applies only to rationals arising from this quotient family, not arbitrary rational approximants.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The quotient proof applies the 1429/1512 floor to rungs e+2 and 2e+2 together with the residual prefix and upper-rung estimates.
Strictly positive weights preserve the pointwise 1/480 margin, while a singleton family recovers the original obstruction.
Substituting rankOneSubrankQuotient e Y=p/q, multiplying by q>0, and taking absolute values gives the stated linear-form bound.
